_comment: Copy to grants-profile.json in the Grants & Contracts assistant's working folder and fill it in. That copy is PRIVATE: it stays on this Mac and never goes into mchatai-source. tools/scan.py finds it by walking up from the folder it runs in. Every key is optional.
_regions: Which sources.json pages and alert lists apply. us = national. Add the state (us-xx) and county (us-xx-county) you live and work in.
_applicantTypes: How you can receive money: individual, for-profit, nonprofit, fiscally-sponsored. The assistant uses this to label each opportunity's route: direct, through a partner, or as the paid vendor inside someone else's award.
workLines: AI assistants and automation for small organisations
digital walking tours and cultural trail guides
document AI: scanned records to searchable, accessible text
_keywords: Each becomes a Grants.gov keyword query (up to 12) and marks matching lines on watched pages.
_keywordMatch: title (default): a keyword hit counts only when the keyword is in the opportunity's title, because Grants.gov matches anywhere in the text and one broad word returns hundreds of research grants. any: keep every hit.
_contractKeywords: SAM.gov title searches (needs SAM_API_KEY in the environment). Falls back to keywords.
_exclude: Hard filters for conflicts of interest. An opportunity or page whose funder, title or URL contains one of these is never shown as an opportunity; it is listed under 'Excluded by your rules' so you can see the filter working. Example: a board member of a city commission lists that city here.
_extraPages: Your own pages to watch, same shape as sources.json pages: {"id", "name", "funder", "url"}.
